## Write directly to streamwriter

Remove `StringValueBuilder` and write directives fields to streamwriter
Save allocation
Helper to FileName unit test `FileLoggerProcessorTests`

Fixes #33946
pr_comments: Why this change?

> Why this change?

It's about the issue #33946 .
Send data directly to the **StreamWriter** and reduce some variable allocation like `ValueStringBuilder` 🙂.
I'd like to see the performance difference here in terms or allocations and CPU

issue_context.body:
See https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/33251/#discussion_r655734742, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/33251/#discussion_r656445769.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/3177376dca6ca0a6bba1d4ab946e77f02547c167/src/Middleware/HttpLogging/src/W3CLogger.cs#L49
> Since we know the only consumer of this data is StreamWriter, can you delay the Format, enqueue the elements array, and format when writing to the stream? This intermediate string is likely large and useless.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/3177376dca6ca0a6bba1d4ab946e77f02547c167/src/Middleware/HttpLogging/src/W3CLoggerProcessor.cs#L35
> More content that should be written directly to the streamWriter.

Hi @BrennanConroy @wtgodbe  can I try a PR ? 🙂
Sure! We'd be glad to review a PR for this
@wcontayon yes this still needs work, go ahead.

review_comments: One of the savings that was mentioned in the issue is that the temporary string from the formatting might be able to be avoided if the elements array is enqueued and the format is written directly to the stream writer via `W3CLoggerProcessor.WriteMessageAsync`. It would require a bit of refactoring of the underlying FileLoggerProcessor to store `string[]`s instead of strings and moving the format code.
Sure !!. I've planned this change for a second PR (on the same issue). But I can work on it and add the change on this PR 🙂
